what_the_eye_sees: Hero at 300 px: a big step up from attempt 1. An octagonal drum stands on a signet, its walls opened by tall arched windows, with a ring of slender pinnacles topped by knop finials and a small purple stone on top. A jeweller would now say 'Gothic tower' or 'cathedral turret ring', and 'lantern' is a fair guess. The window heads still look more rounded than pointed at this size, and the signet walls and shoulders under the drum are mostly blank gold blocks, so the building stops at the table. Face at 300 px: this view fails. It shows a flat, plain square-cornered plate with a square amethyst in the middle and sixteen thin rods radiating from it, with blue marquise-looking stones partway along and little clusters of beads at the tips. It reads as a snowflake, sunburst or compass-rose signet, not as a star vault or an octagon lantern. There is no octagon outline, no dark pierced lights and nothing pointed or architectural, and the lamps show blue, not citrine. The hero says Gothic tower; the face says snowflake. Without a caption the pair does not name the octagon lantern and Gothic cathedral.
changes: Make the face read as the lantern seen from above. Show the drum's octagonal rim as a raised moulding at least 0.6 mm wide, so the octagon outline is visible against the table. Pierce the 8 pointed lancet lights (at least 1.1 x 2.4 mm, at r about 5.6, between each rib and tierceron) through the vault so they render as dark pointed shapes, and make the 8 ribs and 8 tiercerons 0.6 mm wide and 0.45 mm proud, running from the boss to the octagon's corners and mid-sides, not floating as thin rods on a flat plate. Acceptance: face-300 shows a clear octagon, 8 dark pointed lights and a star of ribs, and no longer reads as a snowflake or sunburst.

Fix the lamps. Tint the 8 corner stones as citrine (warm amber-yellow), not blue, and seat each on its pinnacle shaft's outward face as the spec says (Round 1.5, wall 0.3), so from above it sits at the octagon's corner under its pinnacle, not midway along a ray where it reads as a petal. Acceptance: face-300 and hero-300 show 8 small amber lamps, one at each corner pinnacle, and no blue stones.

Sharpen the hero's architecture. Give each drum window a two-centred pointed head with its apex at least 0.6 mm above the springing and a 0.5 to 0.8 mm central mullion, so the arch reads as pointed at 300 px. Carry the building down the ring: cut the paired blind lancets (0.3 mm) into the signet's 8 outer walls under the drum, and make the clasping buttresses with two weathered set-offs on both shoulders (theta about 130 deg, mirrored) stand out by at least 0.9 mm. Acceptance: hero-300 shows at least 3 visibly pointed window heads, lancets on the signet walls and a stepped buttress on the visible shoulder.
